C0: The title page identifies the play as The Comedy of Errors by William Shakespeare, dated 1589–1595.
C1: The text indicates the beginning of Act 1.
C2: In a hall in Duke Solinus's palace, Aegeon pleads for death; the Duke refuses mercy, citing laws against Syracusian merchants due to enmity between Syracuse and Ephesus.
C3: Aegeon remarks that his suffering will end at sunset when the Duke's sentence is carried out.
C4: Duke Solinus asks Aegeon to explain his arrival in Ephesus; Aegeon recounts his birth in Syracuse, marriage, prosperous voyages to Epidamnum, and his wife following him while pregnant.
C5: Aegeon continues his narrative, stating they boarded a ship and had sailed one league from Epidamnum.
C6: Aegeon describes a storm at sea, the sailors abandoning ship, and he and his wife each lashing one of their twin infants to a mast for safety.
C7: Duke Solinus urges Aegeon to continue his story, noting they may pity him though not pardon him.
C8: Aegeon relates the ship striking a rock and splitting; his wife and two children were rescued by Corinthian fishermen, while he and the other children were saved by another ship that failed to recover the others.
C9: The text shows the number 5, likely a page or line marker.
